niche.habitat: Shallows, Sea arches, Sunken cave entrance

body: Babosa (aquatic adaptation: hydrostatic skin, siphon appendage)

chains.trait: Electroreceptive snout twitching toward faint currents
links: Turbid volcanic water blocks sight and scent diffusion
Electroreceptors evolved to detect muscle spasms of fish and drifters
Snout concentrates sensors to pinpoint targets

skill.effect: The creature's snout twitches as it senses hidden prey and ambushers nearby, revealing their presence even through thick camouflage.

chains.weakness: Loud electrical interference (lightning strikes nearby) disorients it; blind to visual traps.
observe: Snout twitches toward moving fish, ignoring visible bait.
Creature ignores visual decoys but lunges at electrical pulses.
Scent trails in fog do not attract it.

journal.en: It hunts by the spark of life, not the shadow of prey.

plausibility.summary: F20 explicitly favours non-visual prey detection in turbid volcanic shallows; ampullary electroreception detects the weak dipole fields of muscle activity in nearby fish and twitching carcass drifters. F16 limits aerial scent in fog but underwater chemoreception is separate; ignoring visual decoys fits a primary electrosensory channel. Lightning disorientation is a fair trade-off (transient strong EM noise).
fixes: F20 explicitly favours non-visual prey detection in turbid volcanic shallows; ampullary electroreception detects the weak dipole fields of muscle activity in nearby fish and twitching carcass drifters. F16 limits aerial scent in fog but underwater chemoreception is separate; ignoring visual decoys fits a primary electrosensory channel. Lightning disorientation is a fair trade-off (transient strong EM noise).

analogues.organism: Sand tiger shark and platypus (Ornithorhynchus anatinus): concentrated electroreceptors on the rostrum/bill map prey bioelectric fields (mechanism akin to ampullae of Lorenzini).
analogues.mechanism: as named by the judge; no mechanism or reference recorded
see the cited works; chain wording is the council's own

chains.trait: Bioluminescent lure pulsing blue in dark caves
links: Sunken cave and deep arches lack ambient light
Filter feeding is passive; active attraction needed for nutrients
Bioluminescent symbionts or organs evolve to attract prey
Pulsing mimicry confuses and draws curious organisms

skill.effect: The creature pulses a soft blue light that brightens the surrounding darkness and draws curious prey toward its lure. This gentle glow also makes nearby creatures more willing to trust and bond with it.

chains.weakness: Glow reveals position to predators; cannot turn off in combat.
observe: Snout tip glows bright blue in the sunken cave.
Small fish swarm the glow before being suctioned.
Glow persists in total darkness of night.

journal.en: A star trapped in a throat, waiting for a mouth.

plausibility.summary: Frame the lure as drawing plankton swarms and curious small nekton into the inhalant current of the siphon (combined filter-feeder + opportunistic scavenger), not sole nutrition; allow dimming in combat or restrict bright pulsing to sunken-cave/night niches where F20 vision is already useless.
fixes: Frame the lure as drawing plankton swarms and curious small nekton into the inhalant current of the siphon (combined filter-feeder + opportunistic scavenger), not sole nutrition; allow dimming in combat or restrict bright pulsing to sunken-cave/night niches where F20 vision is already useless.

analogues.organism: Deep-sea anglerfish (submersible photophore lures nekton); in shallows, bioluminescent syllid worms (Odontosyllis) use light to swarm mates—here repurposed as attraction (mechanism: luciferin–luciferase or symbiotic luminous bacteria, as in Hawaiian bobtail squid counter-illumination systems).
analogues.mechanism: as named by the judge; no mechanism or reference recorded

chains.trait: Hydrostatic skin allowing hover-still in water column
links: Gravity 1.05g makes supporting weight costly in water
Dense air implies high pressure environment, water is dense
Buoyancy control via gas bladders or stiffened hydrostatic skeleton
Energy conservation favors hovering over swimming

skill.effect: Reduces stamina drain while stationary; allows slow vertical movement without noise.

chains.weakness: Rapid pressure changes (diving too fast) risk bladder rupture; vulnerable on land.
observe: Creature hovers motionless, undisturbed by currents.
On beach, body sags and moves sluggishly.

journal.en: It weighs nothing in the deep, a ghost in the water.

plausibility.summary: Re-root in swim bladder ± gelatinous mesoglea (Babosa body plan), not F4; keep rapid ascent/descent bladder risk; on land collapse is already correct.
fixes: Re-root in swim bladder ± gelatinous mesoglea (Babosa body plan), not F4; keep rapid ascent/descent bladder risk; on land collapse is already correct.

analogues.organism: Jellyfish (Aurelia) mesoglea hydrostatic skeleton; teleost swim bladder adjusted via gas secretion (physostomous fishes) for neutral hover.

chains.trait: Extendable proboscis sifting water for particulates
links: Turbid water rich in suspended organic matter
Proboscis evolves to filter large water volumes
High oxygen availability supports metabolic cost of pumping

skill.effect: Drains stamina from nearby creatures; restores own stamina by feeding.

chains.weakness: Cannot bite; extremely vulnerable to attack while feeding; clogs with debris.
observe: Proboscis extends fully; water churns and clears.
Creature consumes nothing solid; only liquid.

journal.en: A living straw, drinking the sea's dust.

plausibility.summary: Turbid, organic-rich suspension (F20) rewards high-volume particulate feeding; elevated pO₂ (F5) pays pumping costs. Proboscis/siphon morphology matches name and scavenger-filter niche; vulnerability while extended is realistic.
fixes: Turbid, organic-rich suspension (F20) rewards high-volume particulate feeding; elevated pO₂ (F5) pays pumping costs. Proboscis/siphon morphology matches name and scavenger-filter niche; vulnerability while extended is realistic.

analogues.organism: Sipunculid peanut worms and ascidian tunicates: extendable tentacles/siphons filter suspended matter; baleen whales scale the same principle.

relations.note: (council kind 'Scavenger') Rondo carcasses drift ashore and sink; Sifón scavenges them, cleaning the coast. Rondo herds ignore Sifón unless distressed.
(council kind 'Cleaner') Sifón often cleans parasites from Coloso's flanks in shallow water near the islet causeway.

moments: In the sunken cave, a Sifón pulses with cold blue light, guiding lost fish into its throat as the tide turns and water swirls through the lava tube.

journal.en: The sea hides its secrets in the dark. This one drinks by taste and spark.
It brings ink and bone from the deep; a gift from the water.
